title: Public, private, hybrid and multicloud
learningObjective: Define public, private and hybrid cloud (and multicloud), and choose the right model for a scenario.
foundation: Public cloud: a provider (such as Microsoft) owns and runs the infrastructure and sells services to anyone over the internet. No hardware to buy; you can start in minutes.
Private cloud: cloud capabilities (self-service, automation) used by one organisation only, usually in its own datacenter. Full control, but you buy and run everything.
Hybrid cloud: public and private cloud connected so they work together. Keep some systems on-premises and use the public cloud for the rest or for extra capacity.
Multicloud: using more than one public cloud provider (for example Azure and AWS) at the same time.
engineer: Public cloud strengths: no capital expense, fast provisioning, global reach, pay per use, elastic scale. Trade-off: less control over hardware and exact location within a region.

Private cloud strengths: complete control of hardware, security and location; can meet strict rules. Trade-offs: up-front hardware cost (CapEx), you staff and maintain it, and capacity is limited to what you bought.
Hybrid cloud strengths: flexibility. Keep regulated data or legacy apps on-premises, burst to the cloud at peak, or migrate step by step. The organisation decides where each workload runs.

Azure tools for hybrid and multicloud: Azure Arc (manage servers, Kubernetes and data services anywhere through Azure), Azure VMware Solution (run VMware workloads in Azure), Azure Local (Azure-managed infrastructure in your datacenter, formerly Azure Stack HCI), and VPN Gateway or ExpressRoute to connect networks.

Use-case signals: 'no hardware, start today, variable demand' → public. 'Must own and operate the hardware' → private. 'Keep X on-premises but use the cloud for Y' → hybrid. 'Use services from two providers' → multicloud.

animation.caption: Choose a cloud model for each scenario, then the Azure option that supports hybrid needs.

example.title: A bank's mixed estate
body: A bank's core ledger must stay in its own datacenter (private cloud). Its mobile app back end runs in Azure and scales on payday (public cloud). An ExpressRoute circuit links the two: a hybrid cloud.
After acquiring a company that runs on AWS, the bank uses Azure Arc to apply the same policies to both: multicloud management.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (a free account works)
permissions: Reader to explore; Contributor to create resources
portal: Azure Arc > Machines > Add/Create: onboard an on-premises server (generates a script).
Virtual network gateways and ExpressRoute circuits: connect on-premises networks.
Azure VMware Solution: private clouds created in Azure.

lab.objective: Choose cloud models and hybrid tools.
steps: Cloud models tab: answer every scenario.
Hybrid and multicloud tools tab: match each need to an Azure option.
expected: Hybrid = on-premises + public cloud working together
failureScenarios: Assuming private cloud has no up-front cost
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: Policies are applied in Azure but not on on-premises servers.
troubleshooting.cause: On-premises servers aren't connected to Azure Resource Manager.

troubleshooting.symptom: A burst-to-cloud design fails at peak.
troubleshooting.cause: Network link between on-premises and Azure is too small or missing.
troubleshooting.fix: Size the VPN/ExpressRoute connection and test failover.

comparisons.difference: Hybrid mixes on-premises/private with public; multicloud uses several public providers. An organisation can be both.
Private cloud adds cloud features (self-service, automation) to dedicated infrastructure.

misconceptions.myth: Hybrid cloud means two public clouds.
Public cloud is always less secure than private cloud.
misconceptions.reality: Security depends on configuration; public providers invest heavily in security.

misconceptions.myth: Private cloud removes all capital expense.
misconceptions.reality: You still buy and maintain the hardware.

architectureDecisions: Default to public cloud for new, variable workloads.
Use hybrid when regulation, latency or legacy dependencies keep systems on-premises.
Use Azure Arc to manage hybrid and multicloud estates consistently.
